issues.issue: The Agreement is void unless employment commences by the March 19, 2013 start date, yet the Effective Date is the date all parties sign and the signature page is dated 3/21/2013, after that start date. A court could be asked whether the instrument ever took effect at all.

"Such instructional materials and other assistance as Wells Fargo Advisors in its sole discretion deems reasonable and necessary" fixes no measurable content of the Training Program, which matters because Paragraph 10 charges the employee for its cost. The boundary of what the employer must supply cannot be applied.

"At least initially, you will be eligible for overtime pay" leaves the duration of overtime eligibility undefined, and "as may be otherwise determined by Wells Fargo Advisors in its sole discretion" makes the compensation terms indeterminate. Both phrases are open to competing readings about what pay was promised.

"May lead to consequences, up to and including termination from the Training Program" states no ascertainable consequence, and "failure to behave professionally" has no defined boundary. Either phrase could be read differently by the two sides.

The final sentence preserves all Wells Fargo human resources policies and compliance guidelines as binding on the employee, which sits uneasily with Paragraph 20's statement that this Agreement is the entire understanding and with Paragraph 8's writing-and-signature requirement for modifications. A court could be asked which document governs a conflicting term.

The disclaimer that "you are not hired for any specified term or duration pursuant to a contract of employment" is hard to square with Paragraph 10(b)(i), which conditions forgiveness of Training Costs on five years of continuous employment and so attaches a financial term to a fixed period. A court could be asked whether the repayment obligation survives an at-will termination.

The statement that the Agreement "serves only as a synopsis of the compensation and other arrangements" is ambiguous as to whether the document is a binding contract or a summary of terms found elsewhere. That characterisation bears directly on enforceability of the operative covenants.

The "synopsis" characterisation and the carve-out permitting unilateral change of any compensation or benefit plan cannot easily be reconciled with Paragraph 20's declaration that this Agreement is the entire understanding between the parties. A court could be asked which controls.

"Compensation earned and received by Wells Fargo Advisors" is ambiguous — it is unclear whether "earned" refers to the employee's earning or the firm's receipt, and "deficit balances (unrelated to the offset of the draw)" is undefined. The scope of what the employee is owed at termination turns on those phrases.

The forfeiture of any revenue or fees unless employed on the payout date is in tension with Paragraph 9(a), which makes Wells Fargo liable for "compensation earned and received" and "salary earned but not yet paid" prior to termination. A court could be asked whether earned-but-unpaid amounts survive.

The dollar amounts of the "Training Costs" the employee promises to repay appear as blank or illegible boxes in items (i) and (ii), leaving the central quantum of the obligation unstated in the instrument. The obligation's amount is therefore open to construction or indefiniteness attack.

The flat rule that termination "for any reason at any time" triggers repayment must be read against Paragraph 10(b)(ii)(A), under which no obligation exists unless the employee joins a competitor within the following year, so the timing and existence of the debt at termination is unclear. A court could be asked when repayment becomes due.

The five-year forgiveness period here runs from the later of graduation and full registration, while Paragraph 10(c) amortises the same Training Costs over months measured from the start of employment as a New FA. The two clocks do not coincide, so an employee can satisfy one and not the other.

"Competitive Organization or Entity" is defined by a list of financial firms followed by the catch-all "any other person, firm, corporation, or entity that competes with Wells Fargo Advisors," prefaced by "including, but not be limited to." The reach of that catch-all against the enumerated specifics is precisely the kind of question ejusdem generis is invoked to answer.

It is unclear whether the one-forty-eighth reduction is cumulative each month or a single reduction, and the text does not say what happens between the first anniversary and "the first month of the second year." The amount owed on a given termination date turns on that reading.

Amortisation runs 48 months from the start of employment as a New FA, whereas Paragraph 10(b)(i) forgives the costs only after five years measured from graduation and registration, so the two provisions can give different answers for the same termination date. A court could be asked to reconcile them.

Clause (ii) sweeps in "all records and other documents made and/or maintained in connection with Wells Fargo Advisors business" without limit to confidential material, sitting awkwardly against the trade-secret specifics enumerated in clause (i). The reach of the general category against the specifics is open to argument.

The surrender obligation is expressed in terms of "Confidential Records or Documents," a term never defined; the defined term is "Confidential Information and Documents." The mismatch leaves the scope of what must be returned open to construction.

The covenant reaches any client the employee "had contact with or otherwise learned of" during employment, and "otherwise learned of" has no ascertainable boundary. Whether particular clients fall inside the restriction turns on that phrase.

The closing words "or discontinuing his or her employment with Wells Fargo Advisors" are grammatically unattached to the verbs "recruit, entice, induce or solicit," so it is unclear whether inducing a mere departure (without a competing job) is prohibited. The drafting error changes the covenant's scope.

"You will be expected to contribute" does not say whether a binding obligation is created, and the amount is left to be "determined after a consultation" with management with no standard or cap. Both the existence and the size of the liability are open to construction.
